extra.message: Student.create() interpolates the attacker-controlled student name directly into an SQL statement before passing it to cur.execute(). POST /students/ supplies this value from request form data, allowing arbitrary SQL injection.

Attacker-controlled review_text stored by Review.create() is rendered without escaping. Because Jinja2 autoescaping is explicitly disabled in sqli/app.py:35, submitting a review containing HTML or JavaScript causes persistent XSS on the course page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: Course title and description values accepted from POST /courses/ are rendered without escaping while Jinja2 autoescaping is disabled. An attacker can persist JavaScript that executes when course lists or course and student detail pages are viewed.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: Student names accepted by POST /students/ are rendered without escaping while Jinja2 autoescaping is disabled. A name containing HTML or JavaScript therefore produces persistent XSS on the student-list page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The students handler performs Student.create() for every POST request without @authorize() or an equivalent server-side authentication check. Although the form is only displayed to authenticated users, an unauthenticated attacker can directly create student records.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Course creation lacks any server-side authentication or administrator authorization check. The template only hides the form from non-administrators, so unauthenticated and non-admin callers can directly submit POST /courses/ and create courses.

The evaluate handler writes student grades without @authorize(ensure_admin=True) or any inline authorization check. The UI presents this operation only to administrators, but any unauthenticated or non-admin caller can directly submit arbitrary grades.

The CSRF validation middleware is commented out. Hidden CSRF fields are generated in templates but never validated, allowing cross-site requests to invoke state-changing POST endpoints, including authenticated logout.

Successful login adds user_id to the existing anonymous session without invalidating or rotating its session identifier. An attacker who fixes or obtains that pre-authentication identifier can reuse it after the victim logs in and hijack the authenticated session.

RedisStorage explicitly creates the session cookie with httponly=False. Client-side JavaScript can read the session identifier; the confirmed stored XSS vulnerabilities can therefore steal sessions and enable account hijacking.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag

extra.message: Passwords are hashed using a single unsalted MD5 operation. MD5 is extremely fast and provides no work factor or per-user salt, making recovered password hashes susceptible to rainbow-table and high-speed brute-force attacks.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-759: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt

extra.message: The login handler accepts and verifies an unlimited number of username/password attempts. There is no per-account or per-client throttling, delay, lockout, or attempt counter, enabling automated password guessing against all accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The network-facing aiohttp application is unconditionally initialized in debug mode. Unhandled exceptions, which can be triggered through malformed POST data such as omitted required fields, return detailed traceback information and expose internal file paths and implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The database initialization migration creates an enabled administrator account with the hardcoded username and password superadmin. Dockerfile.db installs this migration into the normal database initialization path, so every deployment receives publicly known administrator credentials.

The default configuration loaded by sqli/app.py contains the hardcoded PostgreSQL password 'postgres'. Committing and reusing this credential exposes the database wherever the default configuration is deployed.
